title: submission-meta/v2
description: v2 (2026-10-10, F25-R1; D-23 v3.37): adds `automation`, the structured disclosure the registry asks for (method, models, framework required; cost optional), beside v1's free `tooling` strings, which stay. Optional here because a hand-written block may omit it; the service requires it of every proof, partial and alternate (F25-R2). v1 could not be edited (D-34). The opn-submission block a service-opened pull request carries in its body (F07-R2), beside the opn-precheck-attestation block D-4's bounce rule reads. It declares who submitted, which of D-12's five artifacts this is, and the model and tooling D-23 requires disclosed; the authoritative attestation copies those forward. The block is not evidentiary — the gate re-derives every verdict — and a hand-opened pull request without one is gated exactly the same, with its tooling recorded undeclared (F07-R13).

submission_id.description: The service's id for this submission (ULID, as precheck job ids are)

pseudonym.description: What the ledger shows (D-19); the network stores no other name

proof_kind.description: How the identity was proven (D-19): a GitHub account, or a tutorial proof

artifact_type.description: D-12's five resolution artifacts; reduction is a partial with one hole (F07-Q1)

tooling.description: As declared by the submitter (D-23); never verified, never a gate input

precheck_job_id.description: The precheck job whose passing attestation this submission is bound to (F07-R1)

automation.description: D-23 v3.37: how the artifact was produced, declared by the submitter and never verified. `method`, `models` and `framework` are required of every proof, partial and alternate (the service refuses a submission without them before any pull request opens, F25-R2); the rest is optional, and cost is what an agent can count — wall time, tokens, hardware, a free spend string — never a dollar figure a subscription cannot give.

method.description: Palomar's vocabulary: `manual`, a person wrote it; `copilot`, a person wrote it with model suggestions; `agent`, an agent wrote it under a person's direction; `autonomous`, an agent ran unattended; `other`.

models.description: Every model that contributed, by the name its provider publishes (e.g. `claude-fable-5-1`).

framework.description: The harness or framework the models ran in, with its version where known (e.g. `Claude Code 2.1`).

wall_time.description: How long the work took, in the submitter's words (e.g. `about 40 minutes`).

tokens.description: Total tokens the models consumed and produced, when the harness reports them.

hardware.description: What it ran on (e.g. `one laptop; hosted models`).

spend.description: What it cost, in the submitter's words: `subscription`, `$12.40`, `unknown`.
